Count.description: Nonnegative byte or record count in the 64-bit target address width.

Errno.description: Positive Linux kernel error number in the range 1 through 4095.

BorrowedFd.description: Descriptor available during a borrow without ownership transfer.

invariants.statement: The caller keeps the descriptor open throughout the borrow.

OwnedFd.description: Exclusive responsibility for closing a Linux descriptor.

invariants.statement: The descriptor is open and held by one owner until ownership is consumed.

ChildPid.description: Identifier of a child created in this process.

invariants.statement: At creation the PID is positive. Waiting requires an exclusive live token and coordinated reaping with other process waiters.

WriteBuffer.description: Exclusive writable byte slice. Its length determines the request count.

ReadBuffer.description: Shared readable byte slice. Its length determines the request count.

WriteBuffers.description: Ordered writable byte slices. The slices are disjoint for the duration of the call.

CString.description: Borrowed NUL-terminated byte sequence with no interior NUL.

CStringVector.description: Borrowed sequence of NUL-terminated byte strings, converted by the adapter to a NULL-terminated vector of pointers.

PollEntry.description: Logical poll entry that does not expose target padding or writable descriptor fields.

invariants.statement: The descriptor remains live for the lifetime of its entry. Returned events belong to the last successful observation.

PollEntries.description: Exclusive ordered array of logical poll entries.

Directory.description: Directory relative to which openat resolves a relative path.

OpenOptions.description: Linux open options with a mode for creation.

invariants.statement: Flags and mode have the declared widths. The kernel validates their applicability.

SocketAddrV4.description: IPv4 address and port as logical values. The adapter encodes the Linux socket address layout.

invariants.statement: Address covers exactly four octets and port is a value between zero and 65535.

ExecImage.description: References naming a replacement executable and its argument and environment arrays.

invariants.statement: argv has at least one entry. The entries and vectors remain valid until the execve attempt.

WaitStatus.description: Raw 32-bit Linux child status with helpers for normal exit.

invariants.statement: The status was initialized by the kernel for a matching child before it becomes observable.

ReadResult.description: One read outcome with actual progress, a zero-return observation for a nonempty request, or a failure.

WriteResult.description: One write outcome with actual progress or a failure.

OpenResult.description: New owned descriptor or a failure.

UnitResult.description: Successful operation without a value or a failure.

PipeResult.description: Read and write ends with separate ownership or a failure.

PollResult.description: Ready record count or a failure.

ForkResult.description: Child identifier or a failure before creation.

WaitResult.description: Wait outcome with status, no new status, or a failure.

Timespec.description: Linux timespec with seconds and a normalized fractional second.

invariants.statement: Nanoseconds are at least zero and less than 1000000000 before public observation.

TimeResult.description: Kernel clock observation or a failure.

ExecError.description: The execve provider returns only through a failure variant.

CountResult.description: The kernel-populated byte count or a failure.

I32Result.description: Signed 32-bit native observation or a failure.

U32Result.description: Unsigned 32-bit native observation or a failure.

BoolResult.description: Boolean native observation or a failure.

SleepResult.description: Completed sleep, an interruption with the remaining time, or another failure.

TimerSpec.description: Interval and initial expiration for a Linux timer.

invariants.statement: Both member values have canonical nanoseconds before the timer structure becomes visible.

TimerResult.description: Observed timer interval/expiration pair or a failure.

EpollEvent.description: Logical event mask and user data, marshaled into the separate packed Linux UAPI layout.

invariants.statement: The event mask is 32 bits and the user data is 64 bits. Neither value depends on native padding.

EpollOutput.description: Exclusive ordered writable event slots for an epoll wait.

UtsName.description: Linux UTS identity strings in the caller's UTS namespace.

invariants.statement: Each public field comes from a NUL-terminated fixed 65-byte native field.

LoadValues.description: Raw kernel load estimates for one, five and fifteen minutes in that order.

SystemInfo.description: Linux x86-64 system information, preserving raw counters and memory unit.

invariants.statement: All public fields originate in one initialized kernel record. Memory quantities need scaling by the reported memory unit when expressing bytes.

RandomMode.description: Blocking behavior of the Linux getrandom provider.

UtsResult.description: Observed UTS identity or a failure.

SystemInfoResult.description: Observed system counters or a failure.

Protection.description: Readable logical memory states with optional write access.

Advice.description: Advisory policy for an anonymous private mapping.

Mapping.description: Owned anonymous private memory range with a tracked protection profile.

invariants.statement: The mapping has one owner and a positive logical length. The provider does not alias a live range through a writable public reference.
A mutable byte observation is only available when the provider has established writable protection for the whole range.
The declared mapping profile is always readable. Users of the external kernel mapping API must preserve this premise.

UnmapResult.description: Completion or failure with recoverable ownership.

UnmapFailure.description: Error data associated with a retained mapping.

UtsNamespace.description: Unforgeable thread-affine authority for the private UTS namespace made current by unshare_uts.

invariants.statement: The token is valid on the creating thread while that thread continues to use the associated private UTS namespace. Later namespace transitions invalidate the authority for operations on the previous namespace.
A token becomes available only once native unshare succeeds for CLONE_NEWUTS.

HostnameBytes.description: Borrowed raw hostname bytes, allowing an empty value and embedded NUL.

UtsNamespaceResult.description: New private UTS namespace authority or a failure.

U64Result.description: Unsigned 64-bit native observation or a failure.

FileTimestamp.description: Timestamp with signed seconds and unsigned nanoseconds as reported by statx.

invariants.statement: The public nanoseconds field is less than 1000000000.

OptionalU16.description: Present only when the corresponding native metadata field is available.

OptionalU32.description: Present only when the corresponding native metadata field is available.

OptionalU64.description: Present only when the corresponding native metadata field is available.

OptionalFileTimestamp.description: Present only when the corresponding native metadata field is available.

FileMetadata.description: Selected statx metadata and the kernel-reported availability mask.

invariants.statement: A field is exposed only when its corresponding availability bit is set. All exposed timestamps have normalized nanoseconds.

MetadataResult.description: Observed file metadata or a failure.

invariants.statement: The nonempty NUL-terminated name borrows the initialized directory buffer prefix. The signed next_offset is an opaque filesystem position cookie. Kind zero indicates no known type.

DirectoryEntries.description: Directory entries in native record order; names borrow the output buffer.

DirectoryResult.description: Ordered directory records or a failure.

Timeval.description: Kernel time value with seconds and normalized fractional microseconds.

invariants.statement: A publicly observed microseconds field is at least zero and less than 1000000.

TimevalResult.description: Observed wall-clock time or a failure.

I64Result.description: Signed 64-bit native observation or a failure.

ClockSleepMode.description: A relative duration or absolute clock deadline.

ClockSleepResult.description: Completion, an interruption with an optional remainder, or another failure.

Limit.description: Finite resource limit or the native infinity sentinel.

Rlimit.description: Soft and hard kernel resource limits for one resource.

invariants.statement: Both values come from the same kernel resource record and encode the infinity sentinel as Unlimited.

RlimitResult.description: Observed resource limits or a failure.

SchedulePolicyResult.description: Observed scheduling policy or a failure.

ResourceUsageResult.description: Observed CPU time and kernel resource counters or a failure.

SocketPairResult.description: Two independently owned connected stream descriptors or a failure.

IoUringInfo.description: Validated queue sizes and feature bits returned by ring setup.

invariants.statement: Queue sizes and feature flags derive from the kernel-initialized parameter record for the new ring.

IoUringSetupResult.description: Owned ring descriptor and setup information or a failure.

IoUringOpcode.description: One observed kernel opcode and its probe flags.

invariants.statement: The opcode number and flags originate in the native record's validated returned prefix.

IoUringOpcodes.description: Initialized opcode records in native kernel order.

IoUringProbe.description: A ring's reported last opcode and ordered opcode capability records.

invariants.statement: The operation list is limited to the initialized returned prefix. Capability bits describe the kernel observation and do not confer provider support for submitting work.

IoUringProbeResult.description: Observed io_uring capability records or a failure.

BpfArray.description: Owned descriptor for a plain Linux BPF array with U32 indexes and U64 values.

invariants.statement: The map has 1 through 1024 entries and the resource manages one descriptor. Dropping the owner releases its descriptor.
The map's native kind is ARRAY, with fixed four-byte keys and eight-byte values.

BpfArrayResult.description: Owned plain BPF array or a failure.

invariants.statement: The observable nanosecond component has a value below 1000000000.

FileStat.description: Metadata read from one native struct stat result.

invariants.statement: Each logical field originates in the initialized native record. All timestamp fractions are checked before return.

SchedulePolicy.description: Preserved Linux scheduling policy code and reset-on-fork flag.

invariants.statement: The numeric policy code excludes the separately decoded reset-on-fork bit.

PriorityKind.description: Named native target selection rules for the priority query.

UsageScope.description: User and system resource accounting scope.

UsageTime.description: Nonnegative resource accounting duration with normalized microseconds.

invariants.statement: The seconds value represents a nonnegative CPU duration. Microseconds are at most 999999.

ResourceUsage.description: Kernel resource accounting counters and CPU times for one observed scope.

invariants.statement: User and system durations and all signed counters come from one native rusage record and describe the selected scope.

FileAdvice.description: Named native advice values accepted by fadvise64.

SyncFileRangeFlags.description: Combination of the Linux WAIT_BEFORE, WRITE and WAIT_AFTER file range flags.

invariants.statement: Only values with the three declared flag bits can be constructed in this profile.

OffsetReference.description: Exclusive in/out signed offset slot for copy_file_range.

invariants.statement: The caller gives exclusive access to the logical signed byte offset for the duration of the native request.

OptionalOffsetReference.description: Explicit mutable offset or implicit open-file-description position.

CpuLocation.description: Observed logical CPU and NUMA node identifiers.

invariants.statement: Both identifiers come from the same initialized native observation. They do not promise future execution location.

CpuLocationResult.description: Observed CPU and NUMA node or a failure.

UdpSocket4.description: Owned IPv4 UDP socket descriptor with close-on-exec set at allocation.

invariants.statement: The descriptor comes from AF_INET with SOCK_DGRAM and IPPROTO_UDP. Its owner is responsible for release when the resource is no longer needed.

UdpSocketResult.description: Owned IPv4 UDP descriptor or a failure.

Datagram4.description: One IPv4 UDP packet's source, written prefix and original datagram length.

invariants.statement: Bytes written is the minimum of caller buffer capacity and full datagram length. The result can report zero for an empty received packet without indicating EOF.
The source is decoded from the validated native IPv4 output record.

DatagramResult.description: An observed IPv4 datagram or a failure.

ThreadName.description: A Linux thread name exposed through a NUL-terminated byte string.

invariants.statement: The result contains a terminator within the 16-byte native command output. The logical name has at most 15 bytes.

ThreadNameResult.description: Observed current thread name or a failure.

QueueName.description: A validated borrowed POSIX message queue name.

invariants.statement: The next component after the leading slash is nonempty, at most 255 bytes, and contains no additional slash. Dot and dot-dot are excluded. The adapter strips the leading slash for the native Linux ABI.

QueueLimits.description: Maximum message count and maximum bytes per message for one queue.

invariants.statement: Both values are positive and fit a signed 64-bit native long. The kernel may impose stricter configured and namespace bounds.

OptionalQueueLimits.description: Use selected limits or Linux's queue defaults.

OptionalQueueCreate.description: Select opening an existing queue or requesting queue creation.

OptionalNonblocking.description: Optional change to an open message queue description's O_NONBLOCK flag.

QueueCreate.description: Creation mode, exclusive option and optional configured limits.

invariants.statement: The provider rejects permissions beyond the declared 0 through 0777 mode range. The kernel applies the current umask when creating a queue.

QueueOpen.description: Access and blocking properties with optional creation.

invariants.statement: Access is one declared mode. Optional creation carries the requested queue permissions and limits.

MessageQueue.description: Owned descriptor for an opened Linux POSIX message queue.

invariants.statement: Exactly one owner retains the descriptor. Closing the owner releases the descriptor. Removing a queue name does not release any owner's open descriptor.

QueueResult.description: Owned message queue descriptor or a failure.

ReceivedMessage.description: Received payload prefix length and Linux queue priority.

invariants.statement: Length describes the initialized prefix and does not exceed the caller's writable capacity. Priority is below 32768. Length zero is a valid complete message.

MessageReceiveResult.description: Received payload count and priority or a failure.

QueueAttributes.description: Observed nonblocking state, configured limits and queued-message count.

invariants.statement: The message count is no greater than the stated positive maximum. The native nonblocking bit is the only public flag in this profile.

QueueAttributeResult.description: Observed previous queue attributes or a failure.

PrivateMountNamespace.description: Thread-affine authority for a newly created private mount namespace.

invariants.statement: The token is available only after successful native mount namespace entry and recursive private propagation. It identifies the current namespace on the thread that created it. Dropping the token leaves that thread in the new namespace.
The namespace is exclusively borrowed while one tracked tmpfs attachment exists. External namespace or mount changes that bypass this model fall outside the attachment assumptions.

MountSyscallFailure.description: Decoded Linux error or adapter error at one mount lifecycle step.

MountNamespaceResult.description: A private namespace token or the observed failure step.

MountedTmpfs.description: Owned handle anchoring a tmpfs root, with an exclusive lend of its private mount namespace.

invariants.statement: An active handle anchors the tmpfs created by this operation. External namespace replacement, overmounts and edits to the claimed isolation remain outside the profile.

The handle owns its descriptor and records whether the attachment remains active. Explicit detach observes the result. Dropping an active handle makes a best-effort detach through a usable namespace token. If that fails the token is marked unusable.

MountedTmpfsResult.description: Owned tmpfs attachment or a failure.

OptionalMountFailure.description: Optional failed native detach step reported with cwd restoration failure.

UnmountTmpfsResult.description: Observed anchored detach and directory restoration outcome.

XattrMode.description: Selected Linux extended attribute update behavior.

OptionalXattrBuffer.description: No buffer for a length query or a writable byte slice.

StreamReadOutcome.description: Observed stream progress or a zero result for a nonempty request.

ReceivedStreamMessage.description: One payload-only stream receive with exact returned status bits.

invariants.statement: Progress identifies the initialized prefix of the ordered writable slices. The reported count never exceeds the total supplied capacity.
Data and control truncation describe the corresponding native flag bits separately. Other returned bits are preserved without interpretation.

StreamMessageResult.description: Received payload progress and message flags or a failure.

CPathResult.description: Borrowed initialized path or a failure.

U16Result.description: Observed unsigned 16-bit value or a failure.

GroupBuffer.description: Exclusive writable U32 slots for Linux group identifiers.

ChildPidFd.description: Owned descriptor pinning the Linux identity of a provider-managed child.

invariants.statement: The descriptor comes from a live ChildPid token at open time, remains tied to that kernel process identity and does not acquire a new process when its numeric PID is reused.
The resource owns a close-on-exec descriptor and dropping the owner closes it. The caller separately retains responsibility for reaping the child.

ChildPidFdResult.description: Owned pidfd for one child or a failure.

ChildSignal.description: Selected Linux child-control operations through a retained pidfd.

UserSignal.description: One selected user signal in the scoped profile.

UserSignals.description: Typed mask limited to SIGUSR1 and SIGUSR2.

invariants.statement: The value selects SIGUSR1, SIGUSR2 or both. Native mask conversion leaves all other signal bits clear.

CurrentThreadSignalScope.description: Lexically bounded, thread-affine authority for selected user signals.

invariants.statement: The capability is available only during the body callback after successful mask setup on the current thread. It cannot outlive the callback or transfer to another thread.
The selected signal bits remain blocked for the scope while the caller leaves this scope's mask management to the provider.

SignalScopeCallback.description: A single-invocation callback taking a borrowed CurrentThreadSignalScope and returning a value T independent of the capability lifetime.

SignalScopeBodyValue.description: The T returned by the supplied SignalScopeCallback; capability-dependent borrows cannot escape into T.

SignalSyscallFailure.description: Decoded Linux or adapter failure for one signal scope step.

SignalScopeResult.description: Body result or an observed scope setup or restoration failure.

SignalEvent.description: Observed user-signal number and selected Linux signalfd observation fields.

invariants.statement: Fields are decoded from one complete native signalfd event record under the scoped user-signal profile.

SignalFd.description: Owned nonblocking signalfd valid during its current-thread signal scope.

invariants.statement: The resource owns its close-on-exec descriptor. Its lifetime depends on the borrowed signal scope. Explicit close consumes it and dropping it releases descriptor ownership.
A successful signalfd_read observes one selected SignalEvent from a complete native record. A read with no event available preserves the native EAGAIN result.

SignalFdResult.description: Owned scoped descriptor or a failure.

SignalEventResult.description: Observed scoped signal event or a failure.

OptionalCredentialId.description: Preserve a stored identifier or supply one native unsigned replacement.

MicroTimestamp.description: Signed seconds and a validated native microsecond component.

invariants.statement: Fractional microseconds are in the inclusive interval zero through 999999.

NanoTimestamp.description: Exact nanosecond time or one of the two Linux timestamp sentinels.

invariants.statement: The exact constructor enforces fractional nanoseconds between zero and 999999999. NOW and OMIT map to the native sentinels.

FileTimesSeconds.description: Access and modification timestamp inputs expressed in whole seconds.

invariants.statement: The access and modification time values remain separate and lower in the declared native field order.

OptionalFileTimesSeconds.description: Use the kernel current time for both fields or supply explicit timestamp inputs.

FileTimesMicros.description: Access and modification timestamp inputs expressed in microseconds.

invariants.statement: The access and modification time values remain separate and lower in the declared native field order.

OptionalFileTimesMicros.description: Use the kernel current time for both fields or supply explicit timestamp inputs.

FileTimesNanos.description: Access and modification timestamp inputs expressed in nanoseconds or sentinels.

invariants.statement: The access and modification time values remain separate and lower in the declared native field order.

OptionalFileTimesNanos.description: Use the kernel current time for both fields or supply explicit timestamp inputs.

PosixTimer.description: Owned native POSIX timer created with SIGEV_NONE.

invariants.statement: The provider retains a native nonnegative timer identifier. A borrowed operation leaves its owner live. The profile requires caller coordination with external timer management.
Explicit successful deletion consumes the timer. Dropping a live owner requests best-effort native deletion.

PosixTimerResult.description: Owned POSIX timer or a failure.

TimerMode.description: Relative duration or absolute deadline for one POSIX timer.

TimerDeleteFailure.description: Linux or adapter failure with a retained native POSIX timer owner.

TimerDeleteResult.description: Successful consumption or recoverable failure with the original timer owner.

ReceivedDatagramMessage4.description: One vectored IPv4 datagram and native message status bits.

invariants.statement: The datagram record preserves source endpoint, full packet length and the initialized prefix length in the declared vector order.
Data and control truncation indicate their respective kernel status bits. Unknown bits are preserved uninterpreted. No ancillary output is retained.

DatagramMessage4Result.description: Received vectored IPv4 datagram or a failure.

CapabilitySets.description: Effective, permitted and inheritable capability bitmasks of the current Linux thread.

invariants.statement: The fields derive from two initialized native version-3 capability data records and preserve both the low and high 32-bit mask words.

CapabilitySetsResult.description: Observed Linux thread capability sets or a failure.

CredentialIds.description: Real, effective and saved IDs for one Linux credential category.

invariants.statement: The fields come from one successful initialized native query and preserve full-width U32 values.

CredentialIdsResult.description: Observed real, effective and saved IDs or a failure.

OptionalVectorOffset.description: An explicit nonnegative byte offset or the shared open-file-description position.

WriteVectorMode.description: Default positioned write or the Linux RWF_APPEND request.

SemaphoreSet.description: Owned SysV semaphore set created with the fixed IPC_PRIVATE key.

invariants.statement: The owner comes from a successful new private native allocation and is never constructed from an ambient semaphore identifier.
Explicit successful removal consumes the owner. Dropping a live owner attempts best-effort IPC_RMID in the same IPC namespace.

SemaphoreSetResult.description: Owned semaphore set or a failure.

SemaphoreMode.description: Whether this operation can wait or requests IPC_NOWAIT.

SemaphoreOperation.description: One operation in an ordered SysV semaphore transaction.

invariants.statement: The u16 index identifies one semaphore within the selected owned set and is checked before native entry.
Negative delta requests a decrement, zero waits for zero, and positive delta requests an increment. The mode selects waiting or IPC_NOWAIT. The profile never requests SEM_UNDO.

SemaphoreOperations.description: Ordered, read-only bounded array of typed semaphore operations.

SemaphoreRemoveFailure.description: Linux or adapter failure from native semaphore removal.

SemaphoreRemoveResult.description: Successful semaphore removal or failure with recoverable ownership.

SysvMessageQueue.description: Owned identifier for a newly allocated SysV private message queue.

invariants.statement: The owner can only originate in successful IPC_PRIVATE allocation and cannot be constructed from an externally supplied identifier.
Explicit successful removal consumes ownership. Dropping a live owner attempts best-effort IPC_RMID in the originating namespace.

SysvMessageQueueResult.description: Owned SysV message queue or a failure.

invariants.statement: The logical value is a signed 64-bit integer strictly greater than zero.

MessageSelection.description: Select the first queued message or the first message matching the exact positive type.

MessageReceiveMode.description: Reject messages that exceed capacity or consume with bounded truncation.

ReceivedSysvMessage.description: Observed positive message type and exact copied byte count.

invariants.statement: Copied identifies the initialized payload prefix. The bounded receive exposes no original length beyond the copied bytes.

SysvMessageReceiveResult.description: Received typed SysV message or a failure.

SysvQueueRemovalFailure.description: Linux or adapter error from native SysV queue removal.

SysvQueueRemovalResult.description: Removal consumes ownership on success and returns ownership on failure.

ShmSegment.description: Owned thread-affine identifier for a new IPC_PRIVATE native shared-memory segment.

invariants.statement: Only a successful private allocation constructs the owner. Successful removal invalidates owner operations. The resource does not admit ambient segment identifiers.
Dropping a live owner attempts best-effort native removal. Existing attachments can outlive an accepted removal request.

ShmSegmentResult.description: Owned private SysV shared-memory segment or a failure.

ShmAttachment.description: Opaque, owned and thread-affine read-only attachment to a native SysV shared-memory segment.

invariants.statement: The provider retains an address selected by Linux without constructing a typed Rust pointer or exposing read or write access to the bytes.
Successful detach invalidates the owner. Failure retains the observed active state. Dropping an active owner attempts best-effort native detach.

ShmAttachmentResult.description: Owned opaque read-only attachment or a failure.

ShmStat.description: Selected observations from the native SysV shared-memory IPC_STAT record.

invariants.statement: The fields derive from one private kernel-initialized native shmid64_ds record. Permissions are masked to the low octal 0777 bits, and marked_for_removal translates the SHM_DEST status.

ShmStatResult.description: Observed native segment metadata or a failure.

CpuAffinityWords.description: Fixed 8192-bit mask in native x86-64 word sequence.

CpuAffinity.description: Observed or constructed set of logical CPU identifiers for calling-thread affinity.

invariants.statement: The mask covers logical CPU numbers zero through 8191. It does not describe topology or guarantee continued availability.

CpuAffinityResult.description: Observed calling-thread CPU mask or a failure.

GroupExitError.description: Failure variants for a native exit operation that never returns on success.

SendDatagram4.description: One addressed IPv4 UDP datagram composed of borrowed ordered byte slices.

invariants.statement: The destination is IPv4. At most 16 vectors carry one complete datagram, including a possible empty datagram.

DatagramSendBatch.description: One through 32 ordered readable UDP envelopes.

DatagramReceiveBatch.description: One through 32 ordered UDP receive envelope slots, each containing up to 16 declared writable vectors.

DatagramCounts.description: Completed send lengths in envelope order.

ReceivedDatagramBatch.description: Completed per-message receive observations in envelope order.

DatagramBatchSendResult.description: Ordered prefix of completed packet send lengths or a failure.

DatagramBatchReceiveResult.description: Ordered prefix of completed packet receive observations or a failure.

FileSystemId.description: Two signed native words identifying the observed filesystem.

FileSystemStat.description: Selected x86-64 statfs observations, preserving raw counter and flag bits.

invariants.statement: All fields originate in one initialized native filesystem-stat record. An all-ones count can mean an unavailable value. The result preserves it as reported.

FileSystemStatResult.description: Observed native filesystem metadata or a failure.

IntervalTimer.description: Linux process timer selectors Real, Virtual and Profile.

IntervalDuration.description: Nonnegative seconds and a normalized signed microsecond component.

invariants.statement: Seconds are nonnegative and microseconds range from zero through 999999.

IntervalSettings.description: An interval and time remaining for one process timer.

invariants.statement: Interval and remaining are separately normalized. Zero remaining disarms when submitted as input. Zero interval requests one-shot operation.

IntervalSettingsResult.description: Observed interval and remaining time or a failure.

ProcessTimes.description: Observed native process, waited-for child, and elapsed clock ticks.

invariants.statement: Elapsed is a signed Linux clock-tick count with an arbitrary origin and can wrap. User and system CPU tick fields and waited-for child tick fields are preserved as returned by the kernel.

ProcessTimesResult.description: Observed process clock ticks or a failure.

MemoryLockMode.description: Immediate or on-fault memory locking for the owned mapping.

MemorySyncMode.description: Asynchronous or synchronous native sync, each optionally requesting invalidation.

LandlockRuleset.description: Owned Landlock ruleset descriptor for the ABI 1 filesystem-read profile.

invariants.statement: The 8-byte ABI 1 ruleset attribute handles file reads and directory reads. The owner controls one close-on-exec native descriptor.
Closing the owner releases the descriptor. Already applied kernel restrictions do not depend on keeping the descriptor open.

LandlockRulesetResult.description: Owned filesystem-read Landlock ruleset or a failure.

LandlockReadAccess.description: Selected allowed read rights within the fixed filesystem ruleset.

IoPriorityObservation.description: Observed Linux I/O priority class and native data bits.

invariants.statement: The returned U16 splits into its upper class field and lower 13 native data bits. No unknown class or data semantics are inferred.

IoPriorityObservationResult.description: Observed current thread I/O priority or a failure.

IoPriority.description: Ordinary Linux I/O priority request classes admitted for the calling thread.

LegacyAioContext.description: Owned legacy native AIO context for bounded fsync or private-pipe poll submissions.

invariants.statement: A live owner keeps the native context private with configured capacity from one through 16. Successful destruction releases recorded outstanding resources. Dropping a live owner attempts best-effort destruction.

The live owner retains stable control blocks and resources for accepted requests until validated completion or successful context destruction. An unexpected native result can mark the owner unusable for submit and reap while retaining destruction authority.
With outstanding work, the context expects one submission profile. The corresponding reaper removes that work before a different submission profile can use the queue.

LegacyAioContextResult.description: Owned bounded AIO context or a failure.

AioRequestId.description: Opaque identity of one accepted submission in its creating context.

invariants.statement: The context generates the native tag and correlates it with the exact retained control block. The caller cannot construct a native identifier or move pending work to another context.

AioRequestResult.description: Accepted legacy native AIO submission identity or a failure.

AioFsyncEvent.description: A validated completion identity and its native fsync result.

invariants.statement: The event tag and control block correspond to one outstanding request in this context. Its primary native result is translated to success, errno or unexpected return. The accepted secondary result is zero.

AioFsyncEvents.description: Completions in kernel observation order, which may differ from submission order.

AioCompletionResult.description: Observed completion sequence or a reap failure.

LsmModuleIds.description: Observed U64 LSM identifiers in native enumeration order.

LsmContextValue.description: Opaque reported context bytes, including any terminal NUL within the value.

LsmContext.description: One validated native LSM context record.

invariants.statement: Each accepted record has a positive module identifier and a 32-byte header, a bounded whole-word-aligned record length, and a value fitting within that record. Padding is excluded from the value.
The flags and reported context bytes remain uninterpreted and are preserved in native record order.

LsmContexts.description: Validated opaque security contexts in native record order.

LsmModuleQueryResult.description: Complete observation, sized E2BIG observation or a direct failure.

LsmContextQueryResult.description: Complete observation, sized E2BIG observation or a direct failure.

Inotify.description: Owned inotify descriptor with a private generation registry for consumed watches.

invariants.statement: The owner holds one native descriptor and remains live while a watch token borrows it. Closing the owner releases the native instance. Already queued records can outlive a watch.

InotifyResult.description: Owned inotify instance or a failure.

InotifyMode.description: Blocking or nonblocking inotify descriptor behavior.

WatchMask.description: Combination of the admitted filesystem event selection bits.

invariants.statement: Selections are limited to access, modify, attribute, close, open, move, create and delete events in the provider. The kernel can also emit lifecycle and overflow records that were not requested.

InotifyWatch.description: Owned watch token valid within a borrowed inotify instance.

invariants.statement: The token retains the instance borrow, descriptor and local generation. Consuming it releases its removal authority. Dropping makes one best-effort removal attempt when its generation is still current.
Linux can remove a watch automatically while the token or queued records remain live. It can subsequently reuse the watch descriptor.

InotifyWatchResult.description: Owned inotify watch or a failure.

OptionalInotifyName.description: Absent name or a NUL-terminated name borrowed from the initialized caller buffer.

InotifyEvent.description: One decoded event retaining native watch, status and cookie bits.

invariants.statement: Preserve native record order, descriptor, mask, rename cookie and any nonempty name without padding. A negative descriptor can identify a queue overflow report rather than a watched object.

InotifyEvents.description: Decoded inotify records in native queue order.

InotifyEventsResult.description: Observed inotify records or a failure.

DupReplacementFailure.description: Linux or adapter failure while retaining the attempted target owner.

DupReplacementResult.description: Replacement descriptor or failure with recoverable target ownership.

SpliceMode.description: Native default flags or an explicit nonblocking splice request.

VmspliceReadEnd.description: Owned read-only pipe endpoint created by the private vmsplice pipe adapter.

invariants.statement: The native descriptor is the read-only endpoint of the newly created pipe. The caller owns it until explicit conversion or release. The profile excludes externally replacing the endpoint.

VmsplicePipeResult.description: Owned typed read end and independent writer, or a failure.

UserId.description: Native Linux user ID excluding the all-ones sentinel.

invariants.statement: The logical U32 value is strictly below the all-ones sentinel reserved by Linux.

OptionalUserId.description: Preserve this selector or submit one representable native ID.

GroupId.description: Native Linux group ID excluding the all-ones sentinel.

invariants.statement: The logical U32 value is strictly below the all-ones sentinel reserved by Linux.

OptionalGroupId.description: Preserve this selector or submit one representable native ID.

GroupIds.description: Read-only ordered sequence of typed Linux group IDs.

SelectFdSet.description: Bounded readiness set whose inserted descriptors remain borrowed.

invariants.statement: Only descriptors numbered zero through 1023 can be inserted. The original descriptor borrow must remain available while the bit can be selected.

SelectFdSets.description: Read, write, and exceptional-condition native readiness sets.

invariants.statement: The sets are distinct 1024-bit masks. A number present in two sets is counted once in each when both conditions are ready.

OptionalIntervalDuration.description: Absent or normalized relative interval timeout.

SelectFailure.description: Decoded Linux or adapter failure in readiness selection.

SelectMicroResult.description: Readiness result or failure, each with its available timeout observation.

SelectNanoResult.description: Readiness result or failure, each with its available timeout observation.

SeccompAction.description: Closed set of native seccomp action words admitted for an availability query.

SeccompNotifSizes.description: Native notification, response and data record sizes.

invariants.statement: Three nonzero U16 fields derive from one validated six-byte native output record.

SeccompNotifSizesResult.description: Native seccomp notification layout sizes or a failure.

MountIds.description: Ordered observed native mount identifiers in a current-namespace page.

MountIdsResult.description: Observed page of mount identifiers or a failure.

MountBasic.description: Selected native mount metadata from the MNT_BASIC profile.

invariants.statement: The record must advertise MNT_BASIC, match the requested mount identity and fit the supplied native result bounds. Observed IDs and flags retain their native bits.

MountBasicResult.description: Observed basic mount attributes or a failure.

ProgramBreakResult.description: Current native program-break address value or a failure.

WaitIdOutcome.description: One terminal native child outcome with exact exit or signal information.

WaitIdStatus.description: Validated terminal status for the selected owned direct child.

invariants.statement: A successful terminal observation matches the selected child's PID and carries its native UID. A signaled event has signal from one through 64. The core flag reflects the native outcome code.

WaitIdResult.description: Terminal child result, nonblocking pending observation, or failure.

AioCancelStatus.description: Cancellation request awaits an ordinary native completion observation.

AioCancelResult.description: Observed cancellation status or a failure.

LegacyDirectoryEntry.description: One validated x86-64 native getdents entry with a borrowed name.

invariants.statement: The native name remains borrowed from the initialized output range. The offset is an opaque U64 filesystem cookie. The final native record byte is the observed entry kind.

LegacyDirectoryEntries.description: Decoded directory entries in legacy kernel record order.

LegacyDirectoryEntriesResult.description: Legacy directory record observations or a failure.

BlockingSignalFd.description: Owned blocking native signalfd borrowing a current-thread signal scope.

invariants.statement: The handle owns the descriptor and retains the scope lifetime. Explicit close consumes it. The native legacy descriptor leaves close-on-exec clear.

BlockingSignalFdResult.description: Owned blocking signal descriptor or a failure.

PendingUserSignals.description: Pending selected SIGUSR1 and SIGUSR2 observations for the calling thread.

invariants.statement: Each Boolean refers to a bit selected by the borrowed scope in the native pending blocked union.

PendingUserSignalsResult.description: Scoped pending user signal observation or a failure.

NumaNodeWords.description: Fixed 1024-bit mask in native x86-64 word order.

NumaNodeMask.description: Bounded mask of native NUMA node IDs.

invariants.statement: The provider admits NUMA node indexes zero through 1023. The full native query and set encoding uses maxnode 1025 to cover all 1024 mask bits under Linux's boundary rule.

NumaPolicyState.description: Observed native mode and bounded node mask.

invariants.statement: Preserve the validated nonnegative native policy mode and any returned modifier flags without interpreting unsupported combinations.

NumaPolicyStateResult.description: Observed native NUMA policy or a failure.

NumaNodeMaskResult.description: Observed available native node mask or a failure.

NumaPolicy.description: Supported native policy modes with fixed no-modifier encoding.

CacheStatRange.description: Native file cache query range in bytes.

invariants.statement: Both byte quantities have native U64 width. A nonempty range submitted to the kernel has a representable inclusive final byte.

CacheStat.description: One observed native file page-cache record.

invariants.statement: All five unsigned counts preserve kernel page units. Native eviction and writeback state may change independently.

CacheStatResult.description: Observed native file page-cache counts or a failure.

FutexWord.description: One naturally aligned native U32 atomic word for process-private futex operations.

invariants.statement: The borrow keeps the word live at its native address throughout the call. Concurrent access uses atomic operations.

FutexWaiter.description: One borrowed live private U32 futex and its expected value.

invariants.statement: The borrowed atomic word stays live at its native address throughout the wait.

FutexWaiterVector.description: Ordered vector of one through 128 private atomic futex waiters.

FutexWaitVectorResult.description: Index of a notified waiter, or a native or adapter failure.

SchedulerAttributes.description: Observed current-thread fields from the native scheduler attribute version-zero record.

invariants.statement: All fields come from the admitted native version-zero response.

SchedulerAttributesResult.description: Observed scheduler parameters or a failure.

SchedulerPolicy.description: One ordinary Linux scheduling policy supported by the caller-only setters.

ClockDisciplineState.description: Native clock discipline status returned outside the errno envelope.

TimexSubseconds.description: Observed fractional time in the native record's stated resolution.

TimexObservation.description: Validated clock discipline status and initialized Linux timex fields.

invariants.statement: The native STA_NANO status selects nanoseconds for the fractional time and the offset. Otherwise those values use microseconds. The typed fraction is in range for its resolution.

TimexObservationResult.description: Observed timex state or a failure.

RobustListInfo.description: Presence and native head length of the calling thread's robust futex registration.

invariants.statement: A returned observation has the admitted native 24-byte head width. The kernel address is not exposed.

RobustListInfoResult.description: Observed registration metadata, or a native or adapter failure.

Fanotify.description: Owned nonblocking notification group with at most one borrowed inode mark.

invariants.statement: The group retains the marked object's borrowed descriptor while a corresponding mark is tracked. Group teardown discards marks and pending notifications.

FanotifyResult.description: Owned native notification group or a failure.

FanotifyMask.description: Mask composed from the provider's native access, modification, close and open event bits.

OptionalFanotifyFd.description: Kernel event with or without a delivered file descriptor.

FanotifyEvent.description: One validated native notification with its observed mask and PID.

invariants.statement: A delivered nonnegative descriptor is owned and close-on-exec. The native FAN_NOFD sentinel leaves it absent. Native PID zero may represent a task outside the visible PID namespace.

FanotifyEventResult.description: One decoded notification or a failure.

SessionKeyring.description: Thread-affine authority for one anonymous session keyring installed by the caller.

invariants.statement: The token belongs to the installing thread. Releasing the token does not restore the former session.

SessionKeyringResult.description: New anonymous session authority or a failure.

OwnedUserKey.description: An opaque user-key link exclusively borrowing its owning session keyring.

invariants.statement: An active key records its exact kernel identity, description and original payload size. Unlink consumes its active link state. Destruction attempts to remove the exact active link if it remains owned.

OwnedUserKeyResult.description: Owned user-key link or a failure.

KeyReadResult.description: Complete owned key data transfer, required capacity, or a failure.

SegmentBaseResult.description: Observed native 64-bit segment base or a failure.

ChangeRootResult.description: Completed owned-root transition or the observed stage failure.

RobustListWorkerStartFailure.description: Opaque worker creation failure from the provider runtime.

invariants.statement: The failure belongs to starting the dedicated native worker. It carries no caller-supplied worker authority.

RobustListScopeSyscallError.description: Decoded Linux or adapter failure for one robust-list worker step.

RobustListScopeResult.description: Observed temporary worker registration and verified restoration, or a stage failure.

ScopedFileHandle.description: Opaque native file handle bound to one borrowed owned tmpfs and exact source inode.

invariants.statement: The handle retains the exact source descriptor, an ordinary descriptor for its borrowed mount root, a validated private kernel handle and the unique native mount ID. The caller cannot supply or edit the handle bytes.

ScopedFileHandleResult.description: Scoped native regular-file handle or a failure.

OptionalAccountingPath.description: Existing file path supplied for process accounting, or a null native path to disable.

SealedExecutable.description: Owned close-on-exec executable memfd with a sealed image.

invariants.statement: The file's bytes, size and execute bits are sealed before the token becomes observable. The token exposes no arbitrary descriptor conversion.

SealedExecutableResult.description: Prepared sealed executable descriptor or a failure.

ExecveAtImage.description: Prepared descriptor-based image and native argument vectors.

invariants.statement: An owned sealed executable stays borrowed. Argument vectors are terminated for Linux and argv has at least one entry.

ExecveAtResult.description: Native or adapter failure returning from a descriptor execution attempt.

VforkExecResult.description: Owned vfork child or a staged native failure with any launch result retained.

ScopedNativeFailure.description: Decoded Linux error or adapter error at a scoped native operation step.

LegacyUstatLabel.description: Six raw bytes of a legacy filesystem label.

invariants.statement: Exactly six bytes are returned. The pinned Linux implementation zeros these labels.
The signed free-block count has native legacy width and can truncate a larger count. Free inodes are unsigned at native word width.

LegacyUstatResult.description: Observation of the filesystem selected by a borrowed descriptor or a failure.

QueueNotification.description: Register one silent POSIX message queue notification or unregister.

ProtectionKey.description: Owned nondefault native memory protection key.

invariants.statement: Own a validated key in the range 1 through 15 in the calling address space. Drop attempts a best-effort native release.
This provider does not associate this nondefault key with any mapping.

ProtectionKeyReleaseResult.description: Release or failure carrying the still-owned key.

SealedMapping.description: Read-only provider view of a sealed mapping.

invariants.statement: The exact mapped range remains readable through this token. The provider deliberately keeps it mapped until process exit, even after the token is dropped.

SealMappingResult.description: Sealed readable view or failure that retains the original mapping ownership.

SavedUtsNamespace.description: Thread-affine owned descriptor pinning one private UTS namespace.

invariants.statement: Retain a close-on-exec descriptor for the exact namespace created and captured on this thread. The provider accepts no external namespace descriptor or process identifier.

PinnedUtsNamespaceResult.description: New private authority and its exact saved descriptor, or a typed stage failure.

KnownChildDescriptor.description: Borrowed own-child identity and known local open file description.

invariants.statement: Retain a borrow of the exact provider child PID descriptor and live local expected descriptor. Select only the same-numbered slot in that child.

ChildDescriptorResult.description: Verified owned child descriptor duplicate or the stage of failure.

SignalActionWorkerStartFailure.description: Opaque failure to start the isolated signal exercise worker.

invariants.statement: Carries the observed runtime worker creation failure.

SignalActionScopeResult.description: Verified fixed child signal exercise or a typed stage failure.

NumaPageOffsets.description: Borrowed sequence of page-aligned byte offsets into one owned mapping.

invariants.statement: Provide one through 1024 page-aligned offsets within the supplied mapping. Retain input order and allow repeated offsets.

NumaPageStatus.description: One native resident-node observation or per-page errno.

NumaPageStatuses.description: Owned observations ordered by the input offsets.

invariants.statement: Each input offset has one corresponding native node observation or per-page errno.

NumaPageQueryResult.description: Ordered NUMA page locations or a top-level failure.

NumaMigrationResult.description: Number of pages Linux reports as not migrated, or a failure.

PrivatePty.description: Fresh provider-owned pseudoterminal endpoints and the calling process's new session identifier.

invariants.statement: Own exact master and slave close-on-exec descriptors for the pseudoterminal prepared through a private detached devpts. The object records the native session identifier.

PtyHangupResult.description: Hung-up private pseudoterminal or the observed stage failure and any retained resources.

RestartSyscallResult.description: Native nonnegative restart result or a failure.

ScratchFilePage.description: One complete native x86-64 base page of input data.

ScratchFilePages.description: Borrowed content for a private immutable scratch file.

invariants.statement: Provide one or more full input pages.

FilePageMapping.description: Owned read-only virtual page backed by immutable private file contents.

invariants.statement: The live virtual page has exactly 4096 readable bytes from the sealed scratch file. Its virtual address and original descriptor remain private.
One owner selects the mapped page. A readable borrow cannot span a remap that consumes the owner.

FilePageMappingResult.description: Owned readable file page or a failure.

SignalWaitSender.description: Sender fields projected from a supported Linux signal code.

invariants.statement: The fields carry the PID and UID from the initialized kernel siginfo record for SI_USER, SI_TKILL or SI_QUEUE.

OptionalSignalWaitSender.description: Reported sender when the native signal code has supported sender fields.

OptionalQueuedSignalValue.description: Native signed queued integer value when supplied by SI_QUEUE.

SignalWaitEvent.description: Validated native observation of a selected user signal.

invariants.statement: Signal and code come from the validated native observation. Only supported sender fields and the SI_QUEUE integer payload are exposed.

SignalWaitResult.description: Consumed user signal observation or native wait failure.

ProcessAdvice.description: Memory advice supported for an owned range in the calling process.

RseqRegistration.description: Thread-affine owner of one private native restartable-sequences registration.

invariants.statement: Keep the exact aligned 32-byte area alive while the kernel may reference it. Its critical-section pointer remains null and the provider exposes no address.
A borrow can observe the latest valid CPU ID published by Linux. Migration may make that observation immediately stale.
Drop attempts same-thread unregistration. When Linux refuses it, leave backing storage allocated to avoid a dangling kernel reference.

RseqRegistrationResult.description: Current-thread restartable-sequences owner or a native failure.

QuotaKind.description: Native quota namespace used to select the active format.

QuotaFormat.description: Known native quota format or the preserved unsigned ID.

QuotaFormatResult.description: Active filesystem quota format or a native failure.

invariants.statement: Own the exact native mapping, expose only a readable slice of the requested length, and attempt to release it on drop.
The provider leaves the mapped range separate from the active shadow stack and supplies no restore token.

ShadowStackResult.description: An owned shadow-stack mapping or a native failure.

UretprobeObservation.description: Fixed provider function's value and native return-event observation.

invariants.statement: Success reports exactly one return event and the verified fixed provider function result. No native addresses or register state are exposed.

UretprobeResult.description: Verified fixed kernel return-trampoline observation or a failure.

AioPipePollEvent.description: Validated native completion of a tracked private-pipe poll.

invariants.statement: The event identifies a tracked request in the exact context. A successful completion means a zero native readiness mask. Preserve a native per-event error and classify a different success envelope as an adapter violation.

AioPipePollEvents.description: Validated private-pipe poll completions in Linux observation order.

AioPipePollCompletionResult.description: Private-pipe poll completion sequence or a reap failure.
